So the second call is from `parse_fencedcode` at line 2297: `is_codefence(data + line_start, i - line_start)`. The sub-buffer is `   ` (3 spaces) from the fenced code content. But this is in the middle of the document (the fenced code content is `   \n`), so `data[3]` = `\n` which is in bounds. No ASAN crash.

The document ` ```\n   ` (7 bytes) gets a trailing newline appended → ` ```\n   \n` (8 bytes). The fenced code content is `   \n` (4 bytes). line_start=0, i=3 (position of `\n`), sub-buffer = `   ` (3 bytes). is_codefence(data, 3). i=3, data[3] = byte 3 = `\n`. In bounds.

So no crash. I need the sub-buffer to be at the very end of the document buffer such that `data[3]` is past the end.

Let me reconsider. The document always ends with `\n`. So the last byte is `\n`. For `data[3]` (relative to sub-buffer) to be OOB, the sub-buffer must start at `size_full - 3`. The last 3 bytes of the document would be `X\n` where X is some char... no wait, the last 3 bytes are bytes at positions size-3, size-2, size-1. If size-1 is `\n`, then the last 3 bytes are `[c][c][\n]`. For all 3 to be spaces, the last byte must be a space, but it's `\n`. Contradiction.

So the sub-buffer can't be the last 3 bytes all spaces if the document ends with `\n`.

Hmm. So maybe the trailing newline is NOT always appended. Let me reconsider. Wait - maybe the issue is that the fuzzer input is processed differently. Let me re-read the fuzzer:

```c
ib = hoedown_buffer_new(opt.iunit);
hoedown_buffer_put(ib, data, size);
...
hoedown_document_render(document, ob, ib->data, ib->size);
```

And in `hoedown_document_render`, `text` is created from `ib->data, ib->size`. Let me check how `text` is created.
